messages:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started — service=runtime-api env=prod-canary region=us-west-2 canary_percent=10 commit=ac3f4b2 tag=release-1.12.0 started_by=@marta

marta: kicking this off after the maintenance window. smoke expected to be quick, will hold for 20m to observe metrics :hourglass_flowing_sand:

amanda: on it — dashboards up (latency/error/throughput). will watch the SLOs and traces.

tom: running a quick smoke locally:
```
$ curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"id":"resp_01","latency_ms":142}
```

deploy-bot: Canary update (5m) — canary=10% commit=ac3f4b2 metrics: error_rate +0.5% (baseline 0.8% -> 1.3%), p95_latency +90ms (baseline 220ms -> 310ms), health_checks 99/100. thresholds: error:+1% latency:+120ms.

elaine: seeing tail latency spike on /v1/generate for requests with >2k tokens. traces show longer KV-load times. :eyes:

sanjay: interesting — could be related to the new attention kernel selection in this build. can we pin to the previous kernel or roll the model variant to quantized?

marta: hold promotion for now. tom, can you run a focused load test against long-context path and post results? we should avoid pushing to 100% if tail latency degrades UX.

tom: running k6 script now (long-context). brief output:
```
scenarios: long-context-heavy (50 vus, 2m)
requests: 6000
p95: 490ms
errors: 0.9%
baseline p95 expected ~220ms
```

amanda: that p95 is concerning. but errors within threshold. recommend mitigation: reduce canary to 5% and add temporary routing rule to steer long-context to legacy-model for 24h.

sanjay: I'll prepare a model-pin config: model_variant=redwood-v1-quant-8bit commit=bf12d9a. This would be a safe fallback while we debug kernel selection.

marta: agree with pin + reduce. deploy-bot, can you adjust canary to 5% and apply model_pin=bf12d9a for long-context route? (manual)

deploy-bot: Adjusting canary -> 5% and applying model_pin=bf12d9a to route=/v1/generate?context=long (manual authorization required). Action requested by @marta.

amanda: authorized the change. monitors will re-evaluate in 5m.

(5m pass)

deploy-bot: Canary update (post-pin) — canary=5% commit=ac3f4b2 model_pin=bf12d9a metrics: p95_latency 260ms (improved), error_rate +0.6%, health_checks 100/100.

elaine: tail latency looks much better on traces. no new regressions observed.

marta: thanks team — I want a 15m stabilization window, then promote if no regressions.

(15m pass, stabilization OK)

marta: promoting to 100% in 5m unless anyone objects.

amanda: no objections from observability. set rollback-window=30m and automated SLO trigger to rollback if p95 > 400ms or error_rate > 2% for 5m.

sanjay: noted — I'll keep an eye on kernel-level traces during the window.

deploy-bot: Promotion started — service=runtime-api env=production from_canary=5% -> 100% commit=ac3f4b2 tag=release-1.12.0 promoted_by=@marta rollback_window=30m release_notes=https://go.redwood/release/1.12.0 changelog=https://go.redwood/changelog/1.12.0

deploy-bot: Promotion finished — status=success commit=ac3f4b2 tag=release-1.12.0 final_metrics (post-promote 10m): p95_latency 245ms, error_rate 0.9%, health_checks 997/1000.

marta: thanks all. follow-up: ops ticket created to run a kernel-level perf diff and add a canary test for long-context in the nightly suite. ticket: OPS-4123.

amanda: creating a post-deploy eval prompt set to watch generation quality for the next 48h. will ping if regressions. :white_check_mark:

tom: documented the model_pin workflow in runbooks (ops/runbooks/model-pin.md).

sanjay: great collaboration — closing the loop. :party_parrot:
